route.text: Common Application for a first bachelor’s degree; dual enrollment during secondary school is eligible. Prior post-school university enrollment cannot be erased to restart. Bachelor’s degree holders are ineligible. QuestBridge has separate eligibility.

rounds.name: Restrictive Early Action
rounds.policy: Nonbinding; restricts other private early applications and binding public early plans. Nonbinding public, military and overseas plans, qualifying scholarship deadlines and later ED II have exceptions. Decisions: mid-December; reply May 1.

rounds.name: Regular Decision
rounds.policy: Nonbinding; decisions by late March, reply May 1.

fee.waiver: Hardship waiver available to international applicants planning to seek aid; request through application guidance.

testing.text: SAT/ACT required. In exceptional cost/access cases, AP, IB, GCSE/A-level or externally assessed leaving-exam results/predictions may substitute. Self-reporting and Score Choice are accepted; ACT uses highest composite. No cutoff.

scores.population: Enrolled first-year students who submitted each exam; CDS 2024–25
scores.note: The composite SAT cells are blank; section percentiles cannot be added. Historical context, not admission thresholds.

english.text: English exams are optional for first-year applicants; they do not replace required academic testing. No numeric English minimum is specified on this page.

selection.text: Harvard considers academic accomplishment, contribution, talents, life context and engagement with differing ideas. Prepare evidence of sustained work and thoughtful writing rather than chasing a numerical formula.

funding.text: International students receive the same need-based aid consideration. Harvard assesses each family’s resources and meets demonstrated need; personal budget and assessed contribution can differ.
funding.forms: CSS Profile and IDOC; FAFSA only for eligible US citizens/permanent residents. See the alternative process if CSS payment is inaccessible.
funding.renewal: Renew each year. The currently published 2026–27 returning-student process uses CSS Profile, IDOC and the student-completed FAADS; my.harvard lists individual requirements. Renewal instructions arrive in February, with a May 1 deadline. Update for the actual renewal year; these dates are not the prospective-student aid deadline.
funding.exceptions: Aid income-document translations may be prepared by students; admission credentials have a different translator rule.

costs.exclusions: Total is the $95,134 lower end before variable travel; published range $95,134–100,134. Add insurance unless waived. This is not Fall 2027 pricing.

route.text: Submit one Common Application or Coalition Application on Scoir; QuestBridge is a distinct eligibility-limited route. First-year applicants have not completed a full year of postsecondary coursework; review transfer/Eli Whitney routes if prior study changes eligibility.

rounds.name: Single-Choice Early Action
rounds.policy: Nonbinding; generally excludes other EA/ED plans. Exceptions include nonbinding public or rolling admission, programs notifying after January 1, and institutions outside the US. Decision mid-December; reply May 1.

rounds.name: Regular Decision
rounds.policy: Nonbinding. Decision late March; reply May 1.

fee.waiver: The 2025–26 CDS reports $80; confirm the current amount in the application. Common App/Coalition eligibility-based waivers are accepted; QuestBridge is free.

testing.text: SAT or ACT is required for 2026–27 applicants; AP/IB no longer substitute. Self-reporting is accepted. SAT and agency-calculated ACT superscores are accepted; do not combine incompatible ACT versions yourself. ACT Science/Writing are optional.

scores.population: Enrolled first-year students submitting each exam; CDS 2025–26
scores.note: Historical score-submitters under the earlier testing policy; not cutoffs or admission probabilities.

english.text: Required for non-native speakers without two years of English-medium schooling. Listed scores describe competitive applicants, not hard admission minima. TOEFL at-home and test-center versions are accepted.

tests.name: Cambridge English
tests.condition: C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency or B2 First

waiver.rule: Native English speakers, or at least two years of English-medium secondary education, are outside the testing requirement.

selection.text: Yale prioritizes academic potential, support for others and willingness to explore. The transcript, writing, recommendations and activities are evaluated in the opportunities available to the student. Historical C7 categories are not percentage weights.

funding.text: Need-blind for international applicants; meets Yale-assessed full need. Institutional aid is need-based, with no merit or athletic scholarships.
funding.forms: Declare aid interest and follow Yale’s individualized checklist. The domestic CSS/IDOC list is not a universal international requirement. ISFAA is not accepted; FAFSA is not required from federally ineligible international citizens.
funding.renewal: International enrollees do not normally reapply annually. Monitor Yale Hub for any individualized requests; cost increases are reflected in need-based support.
funding.exceptions: Ask the office about unavailable documents or exceptional parental circumstances. Late applications remain eligible. Yale’s US-family cost calculators do not estimate international awards reliably.

costs.exclusions: AidMap sums the six published amounts to $97,985 before travel. Insurance is not included in this table and remains an additional item to verify. Not Fall 2027 prices.

sources.note: Detailed instructions request 2025 income; the timeline table still refers to 2024. Confirm the portal checklist.

route.text: Apply through Common App; QuestBridge is a separate route for eligible applicants. Apply to Princeton, indicating A.B./B.S.E. interests. Less than one full postsecondary year generally uses first-year admission; one or more uses transfer. Dual enrollment during secondary school remains first-year; no second bachelor degree.

rounds.name: Single-Choice Early Action
rounds.policy: Nonbinding. Restricts other U.S. private early applications; exceptions include nonbinding public institutions, service academies, international institutions and rolling admission. Review the current restrictions before combining applications.

rounds.name: Regular Decision
rounds.policy: Regular application round; decisions generally arrive in late March. Enrollment response is due May 1.

fee.waiver: Common App waiver requires counselor confirmation. Princeton-specific hardship waivers, including for international applicants, do not require counselor approval; qualifying U.S. military applicants also qualify.

requirements.submission: Common App, including activities and personal essay.

requirements.submission: Academic interest (A.B./undecided or B.S.E.): up to 250 words; lived experience: 400-500 words; service: up to 250 words; three short answers: up to 50 words each.

requirements.label: Graded analytical paper
requirements.submission: At least one complete page from the last three secondary-school years; original English expository work, with assignment, grade, comments and rubric where used. No translation or creative writing. Submit with application or through the applicant portal.

requirements.submission: Send official TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Duolingo English Test or PTE Academic results directly. TOEFL code: 2672.

testing.text: Fall 2027 remains test optional; Fall 2028 restores required SAT/ACT. Submitted scores must be official. SAT section combinations are permitted within a format, not across paper and digital tests. ACT uses one complete sitting, not superscoring; science is optional on the revised ACT. Earlier ACT sittings retain their four-section structure.

scores.population: Enrolled first-year students who submitted the relevant test; 25th-75th percentiles.
scores.note: Historical test-optional cohort; these are descriptive ranges, not admission thresholds or individual probabilities.

english.text: English testing is conditional on language background and secondary instruction. No numeric admission minimum was verified on the current international page.

waiver.rule: Exempt if English is native, or at least three years of secondary instruction were primarily in English.

selection.text: Princeton evaluates academic preparation and potential in school context, writing, talents and likely contribution. Recommended secondary coursework is guidance, not a universal required curriculum.

funding.text: Need-based aid; consult the financial aid application and award for the university-assessed contribution.
funding.forms: Free PFAA and requested family income documents. FAFSA applies to eligible U.S. applicants; CSS Profile is not Princeton's institutional application.
funding.renewal: Aid is reassessed annually; reapply each year. Awards respond to family circumstances and attendance costs.
funding.exceptions: Separated-parent documentation has exceptions. The 2027-28 detailed instructions say 2025 income, while a table still says 2024; confirm the portal.

costs.exclusions: Published $94,624 total excludes travel and any required health-plan charge. Travel varies; insurance amount was not verified. This is an earlier cost baseline, not a 2027-28 quote.
